posts.topic: Do’s and Dont’s after implant placement
posts.imgContent:
Do's and Don'ts After Implant Placement:

Do's:

Follow the prescribed oral hygiene routine.
Eat soft foods and avoid chewing on the implant area.
Take prescribed medications as directed.
Attend regular follow-up appointments for monitoring.

Don'ts:

Avoid smoking or using tobacco products.
Refrain from consuming hard, sticky, or crunchy foods.
Avoid applying excessive pressure or force on the implant area.
Do not neglect oral hygiene practices or skip brushing and flossing.
posts.description: Following these do's and don'ts after implant placement can contribute to a smooth recovery and long-term success of your dental implant. If you have any concerns or questions, consult us.

Prevalence:

Over 300,000 new cases of oral cancer are diagnosed globally each year.

Risk Factors:

- Tobacco use (smoking and smokeless).
- Excessive alcohol consumption.
- Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection.
- Prolonged sun exposure to lips.

Early Signs:

- Persistent mouth sores.
- Red or white patches in the mouth.
- Difficulty in swallowing or speaking.
- Changes in voice.

Prevention:

- Regular dental check-ups.
- Tobacco cessation.
- Moderate alcohol consumption.
- Sun protection for lips.

Importance of Early Detection:

- Oral cancer is highly treatable if detected early.
- Regular screenings can save lives.

Spread Awareness:

Share this infographic to educate others about oral cancer prevention and early detection.

Seek Professional Advice:

If you notice any concerning signs, consult a dentist or healthcare professional promptly.

posts.imgContent:
Wisdom Tooth Extraction: Quick Facts

What is it?

Wisdom tooth extraction is the removal of third molars, known as wisdom teeth, usually in late adolescence or early adulthood.

Why is it Needed?

Impaction: Wisdom teeth can cause pain and damage if they don't fully emerge.
Overcrowding: Limited jaw space may affect existing teeth alignment.
Infection Risk: Partially erupted wisdom teeth can trap bacteria, leading to infection.

Procedure:

Assessment: Evaluation through X-rays and examination.
Anesthesia: Local or general anesthesia for a pain-free experience.
Extraction: Careful removal, sometimes involving sectioning.
Recovery: Manage pain, and swelling, and follow a soft diet.

Aftercare:

Pain management with medications.
Ice packs to reduce swelling.
Soft diet initially, progressing to normal foods.
Gentle oral hygiene practices for a clean extraction site.

Why Tooth Matters?

Choose Tooth Matters for a comfortable and efficient wisdom tooth extraction process. Your well-being is our priority. Schedule a consultation today for personalized guidance.

posts.imgContent:
What is Gingivitis?

Gingivitis is a common and early form of gum disease characterized by inflammation of the gums.

Causes of Gingivitis:

Poor oral hygiene
Plaque buildup along the gumline
Smoking or tobacco use
Hormonal changes
Certain medications
Health conditions like diabetes


Signs and Symptoms:

Swollen, tender gums
Red or purple gums
Bleeding gums,
especially when brushing or flossing
Persistent bad breath
Receding gum line
Loose teeth

Prevention:

Maintain good oral hygiene habits:
- Brush teeth twice a day
- Floss daily
- Use antiseptic mouthwash
Schedule regular dental check-ups and cleanings
Avoid smoking or using tobacco products
Eat a balanced diet rich in fruits and vegetables


Treatment:

Professional dental cleaning to remove plaque and tartar
Improved oral hygiene practices at home
Prescription mouthwash or antibiotics for severe cases
Scaling and root planing to clean below the gum line
Regular follow-up visits with the dentist

Complications of Untreated Gingivitis:

Periodontitis (advanced gum disease)
Tooth loss
Receding gums
Abscesses or infections
Increased risk of systemic health issues like heart disease and diabetes
posts.description: Unlock the Secrets of Gingivitis with Tooth Matters! Explore our handy infographic to understand this common gum condition. Don't let gingivitis sneak up on you – schedule your dental check-up today!

posts.imgContent:
What are Wisdom Teeth?

The third and final set of molars typically emerge between ages 17 and 25.

Why are They Called Wisdom Teeth?
Named because they appear later in life, supposedly when a person has gained more wisdom.

Common Problems:
Impaction: When there's not enough room for them to emerge properly, causing pain and potential damage to adjacent teeth.
Crowding: Can disrupt the alignment of existing teeth, leading to orthodontic issues.
Infection: Partially erupted wisdom teeth can trap food and bacteria, increasing the risk of infection.

When to Consider Removal:
Impaction: If they are causing pain or damaging nearby teeth.
Infection: If there's a risk of recurrent infections due to difficulty cleaning them.
Orthodontic Reasons: If they're causing crowding or misalignment issues.

Removal Procedure:
Assessment: X-rays and examination to determine the position and condition of the wisdom teeth.
Anesthesia: Local or general anesthesia administered for a comfortable procedure.
Extraction: Careful removal of the teeth by a dental professional.
Recovery: Following post-operative instructions for a smooth healing process.

Prevention Tips:
Regular Dental Check-ups: Monitoring the growth and development of wisdom teeth.
Oral Hygiene: Maintain good oral hygiene practices to reduce the risk of infection.
Early Intervention: Addressing potential issues before they become severe.

If you're experiencing pain or discomfort due to your wisdom teeth, consult us for personalized advice and treatment options.
posts.description: Wisdom teeth can be a source of discomfort, but with proper care and timely intervention, you can ensure a healthy and pain-free smile. Visit Tooth Matters for more information

posts.imgContent:
What is Online Reputation Management?

Online reputation management (ORM) is the practice of monitoring, influencing, and managing the perception of an individual or brand online.

Why is ORM Important?

Your online reputation can significantly impact your personal or brand image, influencing consumer trust, purchase decisions, and overall success.

Key Components of ORM:

Monitoring: Regularly tracking mentions, reviews, and feedback across various online platforms.
Engagement: Interacting with customers and addressing feedback, both positive and negative, in a timely and professional manner.
Content Creation: Generating positive and relevant content to enhance your online presence and counteract any negative feedback.
Crisis Management: Developing strategies to mitigate and respond to any reputation crises effectively.

Benefits of Effective ORM:

Enhanced Trust: Positive online reviews and feedback can build trust and credibility with potential customers.
Increased Visibility: A strong online reputation can improve search engine rankings and increase visibility to your target audience.
Brand Protection: Proactive reputation management helps protect your brand from negative publicity and potential damage to your reputation.

Tips for Effective ORM:
Monitor Your Online Presence: Regularly monitor mentions, reviews, and comments across various platforms.
Respond Promptly: Address customer feedback and inquiries promptly and professionally.
Encourage Positive Reviews: Encourage satisfied customers to leave positive reviews and testimonials.
Be Transparent: Be honest and transparent in your interactions with customers, even when addressing negative feedback.
Continuously Improve: Use feedback to identify areas for improvement and continually strive to enhance your products or services.

posts.imgContent:
Cover — Invisible ≠ Fine
6 things happening to your website right now that you probably can't see. (Dark ink bg, orange accent text)
2
Outdated Plugins
Every unmaintained plugin is a known entry point. Exploits are published publicly — bots scan for sites that haven't applied the fix. Yours could be on the list right now.
3
Bloated Database
Years of post revisions, spam entries, and deleted content accumulate in your database. It doesn't break your site — it just makes every page load slower than it should be, quietly, every day.
4
SSL Expiring Soon
SSL certificates expire. When they do, browsers show visitors a red "Not Secure" warning before your homepage even loads. Most owners find out when a customer mentions it — or when traffic drops.
5
Broken Contact Form
Your form shows the visitor a polite "Thank you for reaching out." It shows you absolutely nothing. Broken form notifications are one of the most common silent failures — and they can run for months.
6
Declining Rankings
Google doesn't send you an alert when it starts demoting your site. Slow load times, security flags, and outdated content quietly push your pages down — and you only notice when leads stop coming.
→
CTA Slide
Which one are you unsure about? 👇 Save this post and check your site against it today. (GA Digital Solutions branding)
posts.description:
Your website doesn't send you a warning when something's wrong. It just quietly stops working as well as it should. 🕵️‍♀️

Swipe through 6 things that degrade silently — no error message, no alert, nothing.

Save this. Then go check your own site against it. 📌
#WebsiteMaintenance #SmallBusinessTips #HyderabadBusiness #WebsiteSecurity #DigitalMarketingIndia #WebsiteTips

posts.imgContent:
Cover — Healthcare websites have different stakes
For clinics & healthcare practices: 4 things your website needs that a brochure site doesn't. (Teal/clinical accent, dark bg)
2
Booking Form Uptime
A brochure site going down loses a visitor. Your clinic site going down loses a patient — possibly to a competitor they book with in the same session. Uptime monitoring and instant alerts aren't optional for healthcare.
3
Weekly Form Testing
Submit your own booking form every 7 days. Not just "does it load" — actually complete it and confirm you receive the notification. A form that looks fine to visitors can be silently failing to deliver enquiries for months.
4
Daily Backups
Patient enquiry data, appointment records, and contact details cannot be recreated from memory if your site crashes. Daily off-site backups are non-negotiable — same-server backups don't count if the server itself fails.
→
CTA Slide — Fast SSL Renewal
An SSL warning on a clinic website kills trust before you speak a single word. Renew 30 days early, every time. 🩺 Tag a clinic owner who needs to see this.
posts.description:

posts.imgContent:
Carousel · 5 Slides — Complete Content

Cover — 10 minutes every Monday
The 5-task weekly website check that takes under 10 minutes. (Checkbox-style icons, green accent)
2
Task 1 — Test Your Contact Form
Submit your enquiry or contact form right now. Use a real email you can check. Confirm the notification arrives. If it doesn't — it's been broken longer than you think. ✅
3
Task 2 — Performance Spot Check
Load your homepage and your most important service page on your phone, on mobile data (not Wi-Fi). If either feels slow, run it through Google PageSpeed. You want 70+ on mobile. ✅
4
Task 3 — Plugin & Theme Update Review
Go to your CMS dashboard and check pending updates. Don't dismiss them — apply them (on staging if you have it, direct if you don't). More than 5 pending updates is a security risk, not a backlog. ✅
5
Task 4 — Spam Cleanup
Clear spam comments, fake form submissions, and bot registrations. Left uncleaned, they slow your database, skew your analytics, and occasionally trigger security flags. Takes 2 minutes. ✅
→
CTA Slide — Bookmark this
Task 5: Confirm your last backup ran successfully. Check the timestamp in your backup plugin or hosting dashboard. If you can't find it — that's your answer. 📋 Bookmark this. Do it every Monday.
posts.description:

posts.imgContent:
What’s Safe to DIY—and What Isn’t?

Slide 1 — Hook

What’s safe to DIY on your website?

Some tasks are simple.
Others can break your site.

Swipe to see what to keep—and what to hand off.

 Slide 2 — Safe to DIY

5 website tasks you can handle yourself

1. Submit a test enquiry through your form.
2. Check that your WhatsApp and contact links work.
3. Review pending plugin and theme updates.
4. Run a website speed test.
5. Check that your SSL certificate is active.

Slide 3 — Know the Risk

Not every update is a quick fix.

Updating plugins directly on your live website without a backup or test copy can cause errors, compatibility issues, or downtime.

It’s like changing a tyre while the car is moving.

Slide 4 — Better Left to Experts

3 tasks to hand off

1. Updating plugins or themes on a live site.
2. Fixing errors after an update or site crash.
3. Managing backups, restores, and security issues.

The goal isn’t to avoid maintenance.\
It’s to avoid unnecessary risk.

Slide 5 

DIY the checks. Hand off the risks.

A little website care goes a long way—but critical updates need the right process.

Need help?

Connect with us

The Industrial Relations Code reshapes how organisations manage hiring, layoffs, and dispute resolution. One of the most discussed changes is the revised threshold for prior government approval in layoffs and retrenchments for larger establishments.

The Code also promotes faster dispute resolution mechanisms through tribunals, aiming to reduce prolonged workplace conflicts that historically stretched for years.

Like most reforms, perception depends on which side of the table you sit.

Have you seen dispute resolution becoming faster in practice? 👇

posts.imgContent:
Workplace Safety
Policy or Practice?
posts.description:
The OSHWC Code unifies multiple fragmented workplace safety laws into a single framework covering health, safety, and welfare provisions.

Why this reform matters:

✔ Standardised safety regulations
✔ Clearer employer obligations
✔ Expanded welfare considerations

The Code also introduces structured safeguards for women employees in night shifts and enhanced protection frameworks for inter-state migrant workers.
At its core, this reform recognises that workplace risks are no longer limited to physical hazards — dignity, welfare, and conditions matter equally.

Do employees genuinely feel safer at workplaces today? 👇

posts.imgContent:
1 (Cover): Contract staffing or permanent hiring? Choose by need, not habit.
2 Cost structure: Contract: flexible, tied to the project. Permanent: long-term investment with benefits and growth costs.
3 Speed: Contract: usually quicker to deploy. Permanent: a longer search, but a deeper fit.
4 Flexibility: Contract: scale up or down with demand. Permanent: stable, but harder to adjust.
5 Commitment: Contract: skills for a defined period. Permanent: culture, continuity and institutional knowledge.
6 Close: Seasonal peaks, projects and specialist needs often suit contract staffing. Core, long-term roles suit permanent hiring. Many teams use both.
posts.description: Neither model is better in every situation. This comparison helps HR teams choose the one that fits the role.

posts.topic: Payroll Accuracy Is an HR Responsibility, Not Just a Finance Task
posts.imgContent:
1 (Cover): Payroll accuracy is an HR responsibility, not just a finance task.
2 Trust: Pay is the most visible promise an employer makes. Errors affect confidence quickly.
3 Common errors: Late attendance or leave inputs, wrong deductions, missed changes in joiners and exits.
4 Compliance: Statutory deductions and filings depend on accurate, well-kept records.
5 Prevention: Fixed input cut-off dates, a pre-payroll review, reconciliation and clear documentation.
6 Close: When HR owns the inputs, payroll runs smoothly. Is your process ready?
posts.description: Payroll starts with HR data. Here is why accuracy is a shared responsibility and how to protect it.

posts.topic: HR Policies: Are They Keeping Pace With Your Organisation?
posts.imgContent:
Checklist (graphic with tick boxes)
Policies reviewed in the last 12 months
Language is clear and easy to understand
Leave, attendance and remote or hybrid work rules match current practice
Policies are applied consistently across teams
Grievance and escalation steps are defined
Code of conduct and workplace behaviour guidelines are current
Changes in law or regulation have been reflected
Employees have acknowledged the latest versions
Policy documents are stored centrally and version-controlled
Managers know how to explain and apply each policy
posts.description: A policy that no longer matches reality creates confusion. Use this checklist for a quick review.

posts.imgContent:
1 (Cover): Performance management is more than an annual appraisal.
2 The problem: Feedback once a year is too late to change outcomes.
3 Continuous feedback: Short, regular conversations keep goals and expectations aligned.
4 Measurable KPIs: Clear, role-relevant goals reduce subjectivity and disputes.
5 Development plans: Link performance to learning, so people can see their next step.
6 Close: Start small: a monthly check-in, three clear goals, one development action per person.
posts.description: Annual reviews work best as a summary of conversations that already happened. Here is a more continuous approach.

posts.topic: Stay Interviews: Listen Before Your Best Employees Leave
posts.imgContent:
Image text
Stay interviews: ask your best people why they stay, before they think about leaving.
posts.description:
Exit interviews tell you why someone left. Stay interviews tell you why people remain, and what could change that.
Try these four questions with your top performers:
1. What keeps you here?
2. What would make your job more rewarding?
3. Is there anything that might make you consider leaving?
4. What support would help you grow here?
The key is acting on what you hear. Even small changes show people they are valued.

posts.topic: Myth vs Fact: Virtual HR and HR Outsourcing
posts.imgContent:
1 (Cover): Myth vs fact: virtual HR and HR outsourcing.
2 Myth: It replaces your HR team. Fact: It supports and extends your team on specific needs.
3 Myth: You lose control. Fact: You decide the scope, and decisions stay with you.
4 Myth: It is only for large companies. Fact: Growing and mid-sized teams often benefit most from specialist input.
5 Myth: It is too expensive. Fact: Support can be tailored, from a one-time audit to ongoing guidance.
6 Myth: Confidential data is at risk. Fact: Reputable providers work under clear confidentiality terms.
7 Close: The right support strengthens your HR function. Ask us how it could work for you.
posts.description: Five common misconceptions about external HR support, and what is actually true.

posts.topic: The Hidden Cost of Poor HR Processes
posts.imgContent:
Panels (where the cost shows up)
Inefficient hiring: Long vacancies, repeat interviews, offers declined, new hires who leave early.
Unresolved employee grievances: Lost trust, lower morale, escalations and attrition.
Compliance gaps: Incomplete records, missed filings, penalties and audit stress.
Common thread: Time. Hours spent fixing problems that a clear process would have prevented.
posts.description: Poor HR processes rarely show up as a single line in the budget. They appear as lost time, lost people and avoidable risk.

posts.topic: From Administrative HR to Strategic HR
posts.imgContent: Use only Description with image ------------>
posts.description:
Administration keeps a company running. Strategy helps it grow. HR needs both, but many teams spend most of their time on the first.
Moving toward strategic HR does not mean doing less. It means building systems that handle the routine well, so there is time for the work that shapes the business.
Three shifts that help:
1. From records to insight: use people data to inform decisions on hiring, retention and skills.
2. From reacting to planning: build workforce plans that look 12 months ahead.
3. From policing to partnering: help managers lead their teams better, rather than only enforcing rules.
Where could your HR team gain back time this quarter?
At GA Consulting, we support HR teams with expertise and practical structure, so they can spend more time on people strategy.

Brain aneurysm are like silent volcanos / ticking time bombs in the head

What is an aneurysm?
It’s a bulge in a weakened blood vessel. It can happen anywhere in the body like the chest, brain, tummy and legs
Some are harmless. Some are life-threatening.

Ruptured aneurysm is an Emergency. Symptoms include
- Sudden severe headache ( often referred to as worst headache of life)
- ⁠neck stiffness
- Vomiting
- Altered consciousness
- ⁠seizures
- ⁠photophobia
- ⁠drooping of eyelid 
- ⁠ loss of color vision
- ⁠bleeding from nose


Medical treatment alone is not enough for ruptured aneurysms

Definitive treatment is either
- surgical clipping ( performed by opening the skull)
- ⁠Endovascular treatment ( no cut / opening on the head) - coiling with or without assistance of stent / balloon, flow diverter, WEB, Contour

Choice of definitive treatment depends on
Size & location
Symptoms
Risk of rupture
Patient’s age & overall health

- Every aneurysm is different when it comes to definitive treatment. 
- Talk to a Hybrid vascular neurosurgeon. Get the right plan
- Because with the brain hemorrhage due to ruptured aneurysm, minutes and expertise matters

Unruptured brain aneurysms may have no symptoms. But when they do:

Blurred or double vision
Pain behind the eye
Drooping eyelid
Swallowing difficulty
Imbalance while walking

It may be found incidentally on brain imaging for some other issue

To define the architecture of the aneurysm, one of the following imaging of blood vessels of the brain is performed
- CT angiogram
- ⁠MRI angiogram
- ⁠Digital subtraction angiography 

Brain aneurysms come in different shapes and sizes
Shapes
Saccular – berry-like
Fusiform – spindle-shaped
Fusosaccular 

Sizes
Small (<7mm)
Large  (>12mm)
Giant (>25mm)

Treatment of unruptured aneurysm depends on the size, location, and risk of rupture.

Monitoring is an option for small, stable aneurysms
Endovascular coiling to seal it from within
Surgical clipping to close it from outside
Flow diversion devices to redirect blood flow

Every aneurysm is different. Early detection and the right treatment can save lives.

Don't ignore the signs.

posts.imgContent:
What is a Coma?

A coma isn’t sleep. It’s a medical emergency where the brain shuts down consciousness.

Common causes

Head injury
Stroke
Brain infections
Drug overdose
Poisoning
Extremely high or low blood sugar
Failure of the liver or kidneys

Key symptoms:

– Minimal or no response
– Eyes closed, no movement
– Irregular breathing

How Is It Diagnosed?

Blood tests, brain scans, EEG, and spinal tap tests help identify the cause.

Treatment

Care depends on the underlying issue—ICU support, medications, or surgery may be required.

Early diagnosis can save brain function and life.

Every second counts.

posts.topic:
What Is Decompressive Craniectomy?
(ENGLISH AND TELUGU)
posts.imgContent:
ENGLISH

What Is Decompressive Craniectomy?
Decompressive craniectomy is a life-saving neurosurgical procedure where a portion of the skull is temporarily removed to relieve pressure inside the brain caused by swelling, bleeding, or trauma.

Why Is It Done?
Conditions like traumatic brain injury, stroke, or brain swelling can raise intracranial pressure (ICP) to dangerous levels. This procedure helps reduce that pressure, restore blood flow, and prevent further damage to brain tissue.

How It Works
A section of the skull is removed, and the brain’s outer covering (dura) is opened to allow the brain to swell outward safely. The removed bone is preserved and later replaced in a planned follow-up procedure known as cranioplasty, once the swelling has resolved.

When Is It Needed?
It's considered when conservative treatments fail in cases of:

Severe head injury
Large strokes
Post-operative swelling
Other conditions causing critical intracranial pressure

Benefits & Considerations

Key benefits:

Reduces brain pressure
Prevents life-threatening herniation
Increases the chance of survival and recovery

Considerations:

Like any surgery, there are potential complications such as infection or fluid collection. However, with timely care and monitoring, outcomes are often significantly improved.

Recovery & Follow-up

Recovery usually involves ICU care, neuro-monitoring, and rehabilitation. Patients gradually regain strength depending on the initial condition and response to treatment. Once stable, the skull bone is replaced to restore protection and appearance.

Every second matters when the brain is under pressure.
For expert evaluation and timely intervention, consult Dr. Rajesh Reddy Sannareddy, Brain & Spine Specialist.
Book your consultation today.

Tracheostomy: What Patients & Families Should Know

What is it?
A small opening in the neck (windpipe) that helps a patient breathe better.

Why is it needed?
•⁠  ⁠When the brain or spine can’t support breathing
•⁠  ⁠To give more oxygen safely
•⁠  ⁠To prevent infections from long mouth tubes
•⁠  ⁠⁠To prevent phlegm from accumulating in the lungs


How does it help recovery?

•⁠  ⁠Easier breathing
•⁠  ⁠Better oxygen levels
•⁠  ⁠Faster recovery from chest infections
•⁠  ⁠⁠Prevent aspiration of throat contents into lungs

Is it painful?
The discomfort is minimal, but the benefits outweigh the discomfort

When is it removed?
When the patient can breathe on their own again and swallowing as well as cough reflexes have improved.

Can a person speak while on a tracheostomy?
“YES — with special speaking valves and once the doctor confirms it’s safe, many patients can talk again.”

Remember:
A tracheostomy supports recovery — it is not a setback.

For specialised neurocritical and rehabilitation care, consult Dr. Rajesh Reddy Sannareddy.

posts.topic: Myths and facts about memory loss
posts.imgContent:
Worried about memory loss? Let’s clear some common myths with real facts.”

🧠 Myth 1: Forgetting names or keys means you’re getting dementia.
Fact:
“Occasional forgetfulness is normal, especially with stress, lack of sleep, or multitasking. Dementia involves progressive memory decline affecting daily life.”
🧠 Myth 2: Memory loss only affects older people.
Fact:
“Young adults can also experience memory issues due to lifestyle factors—poor sleep, anxiety, screen overload, vitamin deficiencies, or thyroid problems.”
🧠 Myth 3: Brain cells stop growing after childhood.
Fact:
“The brain can form new connections at any age. Healthy habits, learning, and exercise can improve memory over time.”
🧠 Myth 4: Memory loss is always permanent.
Fact:
“Many causes of memory problems like Chronic stress, Vitamin deficiency, Thyroid dysfunction, and a few structural changes are reversible with timely diagnosis and appropriate intervention.”
🧠 Myth 5: There’s nothing you can do to prevent memory decline.
Fact:
“You can protect your brain. Sleep well, eat healthy, stay active, reduce stress, and keep your mind engaged with reading or puzzles.”

“Not all memory problems are signs of a serious condition. But persistent or worsening memory loss needs expert evaluation.”

For memory concerns or neurological symptoms, consult.
Dr. Rajesh Reddy

Brain → sends signals → through spinal cord to nerves → to muscles

What Goes Wrong?
• Brain injury
• Spinal cord injury
• Nerve pathway damage
• ⁠Damage to signalling pathways between nerve and muscle
• ⁠Disrupted energy generating mechanisms in the muscle

Result
“Signal doesn’t reach the muscle or energy is not produced in the muscle → no movement.”

Types of Paralysis
• One side (Hemiplegia)
• Legs only (Paraplegia)
• All four limbs (Quadriplegia)
• ⁠One limb (Monoplegia)
• ⁠One or related group of muscles (Neuropathy/ Myopathy)

Can Recovery Happen?

Yes — through:
✔ Early diagnosis and correct intervention
✔ Consistent rehabilitation
✔ Neuroplasticity

What Patients Should Remember
“Recovery takes time, but improvement is possible.”
The extent of recovery depends on the underlying cause, the “golden hour” in which treatment was initiated and individual healing capacity.

For Paralysis Evaluation, Rehub Planning, & Expert Care
Consult.
Dr Rajesh Reddy

posts.topic: Not all brain bleeds are the same — and that difference can save lives
posts.imgContent:
Not all brain bleeds are the same — and that difference can save lives


Bleeding inside the skull can occur in different spaces around the brain.

• Extradural bleed – Between the skull and brain covering. Often rapid, often after injury.
• Subdural bleed – Beneath the brain covering. Can be slow or sudden.
• Subarachnoid bleed – Around the brain’s surface. Common with aneurysm rupture.
• Intracerebral bleed – Within brain tissue itself. Commonly associated with hypertension.

Each type behaves differently, causes different symptoms, and needs different treatment.

Early diagnosis is critical. Spontaneous onset of severe headache or those associated with vomiting, altered level of consciousness, blurring of vision, weakness of face or limbs, seizures should not be ignored.

For expert brain emergency care, consult Dr. Rajesh Reddy Sannareddy.

Heat stroke is not just dehydration.
It’s actually your brain’s cooling system failing, and every minute counts.

What happens if you don’t act on the early warning signs:

Stage 1 – Heat cramps
Involuntary spasms in muscle groups are caused by dehydration and electrolyte loss.
Stage 2 – Heat exhaustion
Occurs when temperature reaches 40°C – sweating, dizziness, nausea, vomiting.
Stage 3 – Heat injury
When sweating stops and skin is hot and dry, damage to the kidneys and liver at the cellular level happens.
Stage 4 – Heat stroke
Confusion, clumsiness, and coma, suggesting ongoing brain swelling and damage, precipitating seizures.

What to do immediately:

Move the person to a cool place
Remove excess clothing
Apply cold water or ice packs
Give fluids if conscious
Seek emergency medical care immediately

Heat stroke is preventable — stay hydrated, avoid peak heat, and protect yourself.

For neurological emergencies and expert care, consult Dr. Rajesh Reddy Sannareddy.

The dentist cleared you. Pain still there. Here's why.

You've seen the dentist. Three times. No cavity. No infection. No problem they can find.
But the pain is still there — sharp, electric, triggered by a breeze or a sip of water.
That's not a dental problem. That's a nerve problem.
It could be Trigeminal Neuralgia — one of the most painful conditions known to medicine.
The trigeminal nerve — which supplies sensation to your face — could be in contact with a normal loop of blood vessel near its origin from the brain.
The result: electric, stabbing facial pain triggered by the lightest touch.
If your 'toothache' keeps coming back with no dental cause, you need a neurological consult, not another extraction
Book a consultation today
posts.description:
A toothache that no dentist can explain.
Pain that feels electric — triggered by eating, speaking, even a gust of wind.
This isn't your teeth. This is your trigeminal nerve.
And it needs a neurologist, not a drill.
Consult Dr. Rajesh Reddy Sannareddy — before the wrong treatment costs you more.

posts.imgContent:
Your eyes are fine. So why is your vision changing?

Blurred vision. Double vision. A patch of black at the edge of your sight.
You see the ophthalmologist. Your eyes check out fine.
But the problem isn't in your eyes — it's in your brain.
The visual system runs through the brain. The optic nerve, the optic chiasm, the visual cortex — any disruption along this pathway affects what you see.
A pituitary tumour pressing on the optic chiasm. 
A stroke intermittently compromising or completely cutting off blood supply to the optic nerve, visual pathways, or visual cortex.
Brain tumours in the vicinity of the optic pathway.

Vision changes are sometimes the first sign of a serious neurological condition.

If your eyes are healthy but your vision isn't, the next call is to a neurologist.
Consult now
posts.description:

posts.imgContent:
Every year on November 17, National Epilepsy Day is marked in order to increase public awareness of epilepsy.

Dos

- Always take your medications.
- In the event of an attack, have the patient lie down on one side.
- Remove any sharp objects that may be nearby.
- Loosen tight clothing
- Put a pillow under their head

Don'ts

- Avoid consuming unwashed or undercooked green leafy vegetables. They might have epilepsy causing      tapeworms.
- If someone is having an epileptic attack, Don't restrain them.
- Avoid putting anything in the patient's mouth.
- Don't make the patient smell onions, shoes, etc.
- Don't give oral medication.

National Epilepsy Day
posts.description: Here are the important dos and don'ts one should know during an epileptic attack. Stay calm and let the seizure run through its course. Share this to make people aware so they don't get afraid #NationalEpilepsyDay

Slipped Disc means my disc has "slipped" out of place

Fact

Although the phrase "slipped disc" is frequently used, discs don't actually move. The gelatinous cushioning between the vertebrae, known as discs, are securely linked to the vertebral column by two strong ligaments, making it impossible for such an event to occur.

posts.imgContent:
Your spine protects the spinal cord while supporting 80% of your body weight. Degenerative changes affect 90% of people over 60.

Understanding spondylitis:

• Inflammation of spinal vertebrae and discs
• Cervical spondylosis affects neck vertebrae
• Lumbar spondylosis impacts lower back

Progressive symptoms include:

• Chronic stiffness and reduced range of motion
• Nerve root compression causing radiating pain
• Muscle weakness in limbs
• In severe cases, spinal cord compression (myelopathy)
Risk factors: Age, posture, repetitive strain, genetics, previous injuries.

Early intervention through physical therapy, ergonomic modification, and targeted treatment prevents surgical necessity.

posts.topic: National Cancer Awareness Day - Skin cancer - infographic
posts.imgContent:
The most prevalent type of cancer is skin cancer. The majority of instances are connected to ultraviolet (UV) light, which people typically expose themselves to when outside in the sun.


Risk factors:

a natural skin tone that is fairer.
skin that tans readily, burns, freckles, or becomes painful when exposed to the sun.
eyes that are either blue or green.
red or blonde hair.
moles of specific types.
a family history of skin cancer.
an individual's experience with skin cancer.
older age.

Prevention Tips:

Avoid the sun, especially during the noontime.
Be sure to protect your arms and legs with clothing.
To protect your face, head, ears, and neck from the sun, wear a hat with a wide brim.
Put on wraparound sunglasses that can prevent UVA and UVB radiation.
Use lip balm and sunscreen with an SPF of 30 or higher that offers UVA and UVB (wide spectrum) protection.

National Cancer Awareness Day
posts.description: Skin cancer is an uncontrolled growth of skin cells that is typically brought on by exposure to the sun's dangerous rays. Follow these prevention tips to stay safe. #NationalCancerAwarenessDay

posts.imgContent: Acquaint yourself with Section 206AB and Section 206CCA.

posts.imgContent: Delivery challan registers the movement of goods.
posts.description: Delivery challan is an essential approval document used by businesses across the globe for the movement of goods. It requires three copies - the original one for the consignee, the duplicate one for the transporter and triplicate one for the consigner.

posts.imgContent: A GST invoice is issued by a seller to a customer on the purchase of goods and services registered under GST law.
posts.description: If a seller has a valid GST number, he shall issue an invoice based on the GST tax rate. It is mandatory to include the name, address and GST number of the seller and the purchaser, HSN or SAC for goods and services, and the type of invoice.

posts.imgContent:
Types of GST

Central Goods and Services tax (CGST) - on the movement of goods within a state
GST collected by the State Government (SGST) - on transactions within its geographical boundaries 
Integrated Goods and Services tax (IGST) - during interstate transactions, i.e., transactions between two different states
Union Territory Goods and Services tax (UGST) - on the transaction of goods and services in the Union Territories
posts.description: These are different kinds of taxes under GST in India. For more such information, follow JDP & Co.

posts.imgContent:
Tonsils, which are lymph nodes located at the back of the throat, become painful and swollen when you have tonsillitis. 

Tonsillitis is a common infection that can affect anyone at any age, but it is more prevalent in children.

Symptoms:

Inflamed and swollen tonsils
White or yellow spots on tonsils
Severe sore throat
Difficulty while swallowing
A scratchy voice
Bad breath
Chills
Fever

Causes

Tonsillitis is typically brought on by a virus, like the common cold, but it can also be brought on by a bacterial infection, like strep throat.

Important things to keep in mind 


Tonsillitis is an infection of the tonsils that can be brought on by viruses or bacteria. 
With plenty of rest at home, painkillers, and drinks, most kids recover. 
Antibiotics are not always necessary for treating kids. Viral infections are not treated by antibiotics. 
Make sure you finish the course of antibiotics if they are prescribed.
posts.description: Your child develops tonsillitis if his or her tonsils become inflamed due to a bacterial or viral illness. Book an appointment with us now

posts.imgContent:
What is Sinusitis?

A sinus infection known as sinusitis can result in fluid buildup and sinus blockage. Colds and allergies are the common culprits.


Symptoms:

Facial pain and pressure
Nasal congestion and blockage
Headaches
Post Nasal discharge
Bad Breath
Loss or reduced sense of smell and taste

Risk Factors:

Allergies
Nasal polyps
Deviated nasal septum
Weakened immune system, such as from HIV or AIDS
Facial fractures (from trauma) that restrict the nasal passages
Congenital diseases, such as cystic fibrosis
Asthma and other reactive diseases
Smoking and exposure to secondhand smoke

posts.imgContent: Bone loss can start in a matter of weeks if you stop exercising.
posts.description: The pandemic has confined all of us to the four walls of our home, but you should understand that physical activity is vital. If you are undergoing a painful condition which has restricted your ability to do, Dr Naveen Reddy can help you in devising the best plan to ensure incredible results.

posts.imgContent: Top tips for Orthopaedic Health,Workout tips,pre workout tips,following #weekend vibes or #weekend workout tip
posts.description: Maintain a healthy weight by exercising daily and developing a strong core to stay fit. Just remember to stretch before exercise and wear comfortable shoes. Book regular checkups at Dr Naveen Reddy's to keep a tab.

posts.imgContent: A safe workplace prevents injuries and discomfort.
posts.description: Optimize your workspace to stay healthier. If you work on a computer, you can opt for a standing workstation and take regular breaks. On the other hand, more manual work would require you to keep an eye open for frequent movements that can cause strains. If you do some heavy lifting, stretch beforehand and use your core muscles.

posts.imgContent: Make your home easier to navigate.
posts.description: By installing handrails and going for appropriate flooring older adults and their caregivers can keep injuries at bay. Slippery areas like bathrooms often lead to accidents. Use bathmats wisely. In case of any discomfort, reach out to Dr Naveen Reddy's by the earliest.

posts.imgContent: Relish the festival of vibrancy and exuberance.
posts.description: Basant Panchami marks the arrival of spring and the departure of winter. Choose Dr Naveen Reddy's to ensure that you stay in the pink of health as you bask in yellow.

posts.imgContent: A good warm up before workout is necessary to limit your chances of injury and mke your workouts more effective.
posts.description: Be faster, stronger and better with a good warmup before exercise. It peps up your body by dilating blood vessels, raising the muscles' temperature and gradually increasing the heart rate. Stay safer with Dr Naveen Reddy's Orthopaedics Clinic.

posts.imgContent: Train under guidance
posts.description: Lifting weights that are too heavy can lead to muscle and joint damage and spinal injuries. In extreme cases, it can even tear a heart artery and have fatal results. Ensure that you opt for personal training to get the desired outcome and achieve your fitness goals.

posts.imgContent: Boost your strength, balance and co-ordination with cycling.
posts.description: If you have osteoarthritis, riding a bicycle is an ideal form of exercise as it is a low-impact exercise. By enhancing balance and co-ordination, cycling also helps in preventing falls and fractures.

posts.imgContent: Your safety is in your hands.
posts.description: On this National Safety Day, let's do our bit towards better orthopaedic health by including and optimum dietary habits in our lifestyle. Book regular checkups at Dr Naveen Reddy's Orthopaedic Clinic to ensure that you stay fit as a fiddle.

posts.imgContent: Stay healthier through yoga.
posts.description:
Yoga creates a balance between physical and spiritual aspects of life and comes with a host of health benefits like - 

Strengthening ligaments, tendons and joints.
Increasing flexibility of muscles
Making the body look firm
Aligning the spine and vertebrae

The list goes on. If you suffer from any orthopaedic issues, make bhujangasana and tadasana your sacred guide.

posts.imgContent: Let's usher in a new beginning.
posts.description: Women have an immense capacity to contribute to orthopaedics despite forming just 1% of the industry workforce and facing gender-based issues. Let's do our bit in bringing a positive change in attitudes, perceptions and the work environment.

posts.imgContent: Smoking is one of the leading causes of preventable death.
posts.description:
Smokers live up to 7 to 10 years less than non-smokers, and their quality of life is also majorly deteriorated. Here's how it can affect your musculoskeletal health - 

Increased risk of developing osteoporosis
Detrimental effect on fracture and wound healing
Poor athletic performance

posts.imgContent:
Dos and Don'ts of Hip Replacement Surgery

Dos

Do keep the leg facing forward.
Do keep the affected leg in front as you sit or stand.
Do use a high kitchen stool in the kitchen.
Do kneel on the knee on the operated leg.
Do use ice to reduce pain and swelling
Do apply heat before exercising to assist with range of motion

Don'ts

Don't cross your legs at the knees for at least 6 to 8 weeks.
Don't bring your knee up higher than your hip.
Don't lean forward while sitting or as you sit down.
Don't try to pick up something on the floor while you are sitting.
Don't turn your feet excessively inward or outward when you bend down.
Don't reach down to pull up blankets when lying in bed.
Don't bend at the waist beyond 90 degrees.

posts.imgContent:
Chondromalacia Patella, often known as "Runner's Knee," is a condition that can affect anyone, not just runners. Swipe left to explore an in-depth look at this condition

What is Chondromalacia Patella? 

It's the softening and breakdown of the cartilage under the kneecap, leading to discomfort and pain.

Causes: 

               - A kneecap that is too high in the knee joint.
               - Weak thigh muscles.
               - Tight hamstrings.
               - Tight Achilles tendons.
               - Poor foot support.
               - Walking or running with the feet rolling in while the thigh muscles pull the kneecap outward.
               - Excessive training or overuse.
               - Injury.

Symptoms: 

- Aching pain
- Grinding sensation in the knee.

Management Strategies: 

- Physical therapy
- Lifestyle adjustments
- Specific exercises

Prevention Tips: Knowledge is prevention. Uncover lifestyle changes and exercises that can keep your knees happy and healthy.

               - Losing weight if needed.
               - Stretching before running.
               - Increasing your activities gradually.
               - Wearing good running shoes.
               - Running leaning forward with your knees bent.

For more info, get an expert opinion Reach out
posts.description: Have questions or experiencing symptoms? We're here to guide you. Consult with Dr. Naveen Reddy's Orthopaedic Clinic

posts.imgContent:
Understanding Bone Cancer

What is Bone Cancer?

A type of cancer that originates in the bones.

Types of Bone Cancer:

- Osteosarcoma
- Chondrosarcoma
- Ewing Sarcoma

Symptoms:

- Persistent Bone Pain
- Swelling or Tenderness
- Unexplained Weight Loss

Diagnosis:

- Imaging Tests (X-rays, MRI, CT scans)
- Biopsy for Tissue Examination

Treatment Options:

- Surgery
- Chemotherapy
- Radiation Therapy

Common Sites Affected:

- Long Bones (arms, legs)
- Pelvis
- Spine

Risk Factors:

- Age (more common in younger people)
- Genetic Factors
- Previous Radiation Exposure

Prevention Strategies:

- Regular Exercise
- Healthy Diet Rich in Calcium and Vitamin D
- Avoiding Exposure to Radiation

Make an appointment today for early detection

posts.imgContent:
What is AVN?

Avascular Necrosis (AVN) is a condition where bone tissue dies due to a lack of blood supply.

Causes of AVN:

Trauma or injury to the bone.
Long-term use of high-dose steroids.
Excessive alcohol consumption.
Medical conditions like sickle cell anemia or lupus.

Symptoms of AVN:

Joint pain, especially during weight-bearing activities.
Limited range of motion in the affected joint.
Stiffness and swelling around the joint.
Pain that worsens over time.

Diagnosis:

Physical examination by an orthopaedic specialist.
Imaging tests such as X-rays, MRI, or CT scans to assess bone health and blood flow.

Treatment Options:

Medications to relieve pain and inflammation.
Limiting weight-bearing activities to reduce stress on the affected joint.
Physical therapy to improve joint mobility and strength.
Surgery in advanced cases, including core decompression, bone grafting, or joint replacement.

Prevention:

Avoid excessive alcohol consumption.
Monitor and manage medical conditions that increase AVN risk.
Limit long-term use of high-dose steroids.
Maintain a healthy lifestyle with regular exercise and a balanced diet.

Consultation:

If you experience persistent joint pain or suspect AVN, consult with Dr. Naveen Reddy's Orthopaedic Clinic for expert evaluation and personalized treatment options.

It's essential for everyone, regardless of age, to be mindful of their posture and take regular breaks to avoid text neck and related discomfort.

posts.imgContent:
Viscosupplementation - A Treatment for Knee Osteoarthritis

What is Viscosupplementation?

Viscosupplementation is an injection of hyaluronic acid (HA) into the knee joint. HA is a natural substance found in joint fluid that helps to lubricate and cushion the joint.

How Does it Work?

As we age, the quality and quantity of HA in our joints decrease. This can lead to pain and stiffness in the knee. Viscosupplementation injections aim to replace the lost HA and improve the function of the joint.

Benefits of Viscosupplementation

Reduced pain and stiffness in the knee
Improved joint function
May delay the need for knee replacement surgery

Who is a Candidate for Viscosupplementation?

Viscosupplementation may be right for you if you have knee osteoarthritis and conservative treatments, such as physical therapy and pain medication, have not provided adequate relief.

Talk to us to see if viscosupplementation is right for you.
posts.description: Is knee osteoarthritis pain affecting your mobility? Viscosupplementation injections may offer relief. Learn more about this treatment option at Dr. Naveen Reddy's Orthopaedic Clinic.

posts.topic: Stages of knee arthritis and treatment options
posts.imgContent:
Stages of knee arthritis:


Doubtful (Stage 1)
Slight wear and tear with no significant pain or symptoms.

Mild (Stage 2)
Early signs of cartilage wear, with occasional pain after long activity or stiffness, but minimal disability.

Moderate (Stage 3)
Noticeable cartilage damage, more frequent pain during movement, joint stiffness, and swelling.

Severe (Stage 4)
Severe cartilage loss, constant pain, limited movement, and joint inflammation.


Treatment Options

Early Stages: Lifestyle modifications, physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medications.
Moderate Stages: Corticosteroid injections, PRP injections, viscosupplementation.
Severe Stages: Joint replacement surgery, arthroscopy, advanced physical rehabilitation.

For more information or to discuss your treatment options, consult us

Early you get treated, the easier it is for you.

posts.imgContent:

Snoring
Daytime drowsiness
Sleeplessness or nightly awakenings
Morning dry mouth or sore throat
Suddenly awakening after gasping or choking
Lack of concentration, forgetfulness, or irritability
Depression or anxiety
Constant nighttime urination
Night sweats
Headaches

Call us if you experience any of these
posts.description: Sleep apnea is a dangerous sleep disorder that causes breathing interruptions. Untreated, it can cause daytime weariness, loud snoring, and more serious issues including heart disease or high blood pressure. Book an appointment now to get expert treatment

posts.imgContent:
GFC Vs. PRP for hair


GFC:

Extracts growth factors from the patient's blood to promote hair growth

Higher concentration of growth factors and cytokines than PRP

Promotes the growth of new blood vessels, skin, and hair follicles

Complements other hair restoration treatments

Effective for chronic hair loss due to various factors


PRP:

Extracts concentrated dose of platelets to stimulate hair growth

Strengthens hair follicles with proteins and growth factors

Suitable for genetic and other types of hair loss

Multiple sessions are required for best results

Minimal side effects or risks, using the patient's own blood

PRP stands for platelet-rich plasma.
PRP treatment involves injecting a patient's own concentrated blood plasma into their scalp to stimulate hair growth.

PRP may be effective for treating male and female pattern baldness and other types of hair loss.
Results from PRP treatment may vary from person to person.
